name: 1729 Prairie Avenue — the George M. Pullman house (K01; refined by T-1881)

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B stone (blue) dwelling (D), large and irregular'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

built.note: The marker: 'George M. Pullman Residence. Built 1870-1876'.

research_note: The George M. Pullman house at the north-east corner of Prairie Avenue and 18th Street, moved off the district draft onto K01 by T-1880 under the draft's own id: the 1911 sheet's main block in brownstone, two storeys over a raised basement under a slated mansard with cresting, its north-west and 18th Street pavilions, the Prairie portico and the south-east block, read through the solved camera of the Detroit Publishing photograph (LC-D4-12551, between 1890 and 1901). The sheet's ranges and stable east of the house stay at the draft's massing as pullman_house_1729_prairie_ranges until T-1934; the conservatory is its own K13 record. docs/RESEARCH/k01-1729-pullman-1880/README.md.

documented_range.note: The 1904 target to the 1911 sheet that draws the house: the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped), and the Detroit Publishing photograph (between 1890 and 1901; after 1893 by the monument it shows) shows the same main block. Its building and loss dates are not read here.

position.symbolic_location: 1729 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1729 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).
position.note: The rear north corner of the K01 main body: the draft's origin moved 2.43 m north along its own v axis, to the conservatory's south wall (lot frame u 43.750, v -5.930 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet, whose own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation 179.611 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line; v runs SOUTH, from the north wall toward 18th Street.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main block read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s20fp-1729-b1 p3) in the house's frame: its west (Prairie) front at u 27.8, its north wall at v 0, where the trace runs at v -2.3 to -3.3 (in the draft's frame) behind the conservatory's south wall (pullman_house_1729_prairie_conservatory, at the draft's v -2.43, which the block stops against), its south (18th Street) wall at v 17.7-18.1 and its east wall at u 0. The north-west pavilion, the 18th Street pavilion and the portico stand on it as K08 projections and the door's porch; the one-storey block at the south-east corner is a K01 rear wing; the ranges and stable east of it are pullman_house_1729_prairie_ranges.

stories.note: Two full storeys over a raised basement under a mansard, as the photograph shows on both street faces; the sheet's '3B' counts the mansard storey (as it does at 1801 and 1816).

construction.note: '3B stone (blue) dwelling' on the 1911 sheet; the photograph shows dressed ashlar on the Prairie front and the 18th Street flank alike.

stone_front.note: Brownstone, the register's material for 1729 (frontage register row pa-1729-5), laid in smooth courses as the photograph shows on both street faces, over a two-course base to the basement lights' heads. The rusticated quoins of the photograph's pavilions are not laid (open in the match record). T-1881: trim_in_walling: the street faces' dressed trim is cut from the same brownstone as the walling, as both photographs show it (one tone), not the paler dressed_trim stone. T-1881 (owner, 2026-10-29: the walls read as red brick): laid in K02's sandstone_fawn, not sandstone_brown. Both photographs print the walls lighter than the house's own slate mansard (the Detroit print's master scan: walls 115-135, slate 73-101, sky 226; Taylor's no. 1445: walls 193-204 against the mansard's 165-175 and the stone coping wall's 197), where sandstone_brown's red-brown reflects 0.75-0.85 of a neutral slate's light on a blue or orthochromatic plate and so must print darker than it; the fawn stone, at about twice the brown's plate reflectance, sits inside both readings. The joints are the photograph's hairlines (3 mm rubbed flush, where the brown profile's 6 mm struck joint drew dark lines that read as brick); its courses of about 0.44 m and blocks of 0.9-1.3 m are inside the profile's ranges as before. The stone stays the register's brownstone; its shade is reconstructed (docs/RESEARCH/pullman-stone-1881/, L-k01-1729-pullman-stone-tone-1881).

mansard.note: Through the photograph's camera: the lower faces rise from the cornice (about 12.0 m) to the curb under the cresting (about 16.8 m at y 240 px), steep and straight; iron cresting about 0.8 m high round the deck (y 222-235 px). T-3157: four round-arched dormers, read on the dormers' own plane (0.1 m in from the cornice's face): on the Prairie face the centre one's light at x 455-468 px (v 11.0-11.9) between pilasters at x 449-477, its crown at about 14.8 m (y 266) and its sill on the cornice (y 299), built as a 0.9 x 1.7 m arched light in a 0.35 m surround at v 11.45; the south pavilion's narrower one at x 502-518 (v 14.3-15.3), built 0.6 m in a 0.2 m surround at v 14.8; on the 18th Street face two at x 592-604 and 618-630 px, which this oblique view puts at u 21.7-23.8 and 16.5-19.0 to within about 2 m (built at u 22.75 and 17.7). The print draws the Prairie dormers arched and the flank ones too small to read their heads, so the flank's are taken arched like the front's; the Prairie ones' segmental hoods and ears over the arch are not laid (L-k01-1729-pullman-heads-3157). T-3158: the north-west pavilion's own dormer, at x 322-338 px on its section of the mansard (v 0.8-2.0 through the camera), built as the flank's: a 0.8 x 1.6 m arched light in a 0.3 m surround at v 1.5 (0.1 m off the print's centre, the nearest the hip lets a face stand), its crown read at about 15.3 m (y 273), within the reading of the others'. T-3161, through Taylor's photograph no. 1445 (data/reference_views/pullman_house_1729_prairie/taylor_1445_album.json), which sees the 18th Street face at about 18 px a metre against the Detroit print's 5-6: THREE dormers on that face, each standing over a group of the flank's windows, their lights at x 656-673, 740-751 and 791-804 px, fitted by rendering them through the camera onto the mansard's face where they stand: u 15.3, 9.45 and 5.2 (s 12.45, 18.3 and 22.55 from the Prairie corner, about 0.5 m each way), each a little west of the window group under it; the two the Detroit print placed at u 22.75 and 17.7 move there and the third is added, each the flank's 0.8 x 1.6 m arched light in a 0.3 m surround as before. The two cameras disagree by about 5-8 m along the flank, which the Detroit print's grazing view cannot resolve; Taylor's governs. T-1881: the Prairie front's centre dormer widened to a 1.1 x 1.9 m light in a 0.4 m surround (2.0 m across), toward the Detroit print's x 447-482 px (about 2.3 m at 15 px a metre); its segmental hood is still not laid. T-1881: the 18th Street dormers at u 15.3 and 9.45 are taken off the main mansard: the 18th Street pavilion (bays.p_18th, u 9.2-19.45) now stands forward under its own mansard over their places, burying them, and the bay kit lays no dormer on a bay's mansard yet; Taylor's two dormers there are an open difference on its match record. The one at u 5.2 stays. T-1881: every dormer's face framed in an eared architrave and hood (`eared_hood`), as the 1890 Albertype plate, the Detroit print and Taylor's photograph no. 1445 draw them: a band up each jamb and round the arch, standing out of the face, with an ear out at each side about six tenths of the way up the arch; the band's 0.15 m, its 0.08 m proud and the ears' 0.2 x 0.25 m are reconstructed at the pictures' 15-25 px a metre, and the broken pediment the plate draws over the large Prairie dormer is not built. T-1881: the large Prairie dormer's broken pediment built (`eared_hood.pediment`), read off the 1890 Albertype plate and Taylor's photograph no. 1445, the Detroit print agreeing: two raking cornice arms at 18 degrees, each 0.25 m deep and 0.15 m out of the face, rising inward from 1.5 m out of the arch's centre with their feet on the ears' (0.25 m over the springing) and dying into the hood's band about 0.77 m over it, so the arch's crown (1.1 m) rises through the gap between them; the arms' section, pitch and reach are reconstructed at the pictures' 15-25 px a metre (L-k01-1729-pullman-belt-hoods-1881). The dormers' faces are the front's brownstone (`dormer_fabric`), where K01's are a pale dressed stone: every photograph shows them in the walls' tone (L-k01-1729-pullman-belt-hoods-1881). T-1881: the north-west dormer (v 1.5), hidden behind the forward block since it was built, is taken off this mansard and stands on the block's own (bays.p_forward.mansard_dormers).

north_bays.note: The 18th Street flank's windows either side of its porte-cochere and pavilion, counted from the Prairie corner; the photograph sees this face too obliquely to place them. T-3160: round-headed, as the print's flank windows read (their arched heads at y 355-365 px over the arcade's balustrade, x 600-660, under 5 px a metre along the face), each storey's laid once at the sash contract's sill and height; the window at s 6.0 moved to 5.0, clear of the porte-cochere's west end. Their moulded hoods are under a pixel in this picture and are left to the closer views (T-3161). T-3161, through Taylor's photograph no. 1445 (data/reference_views/pullman_house_1729_prairie/taylor_1445_album.json; the flank's plane at about 18 px a metre near the corner, 9 at its east end), the flank read bay by bay: east of the corner pier ONE round-arched window on each storey at x 546-561 px (s 5.4-6.3), built at s 5.85 in place of the pair at s 3.0 and 5.0, which neither this photograph nor the 1890 Albertype plate shows; on the second storey over the porte-cochere a PAIR of narrow round-headed lights at x 653-681 (s 12.1-14.0), a pier with an oculus (x 699-716, s 15.3-16.6, the oculus not built), and a TRIPLE at x 728-764 (s 17.5-20.3); on the principal storey a pair seen through the porte-cochere's arches at x 745-768 (s 18.8-20.6); at the east end's second storey another pair at x 789-809 (s 22.4-24.1), in place of the single lights at s 21.5 and 24.5 there. The second storey's lights stand higher on this flank than the Prairie front's: rendered through the camera at the front's 7.7 m sill they fall 15-20 px (about 0.8 m) under the photograph's, whose heads stand about 1 m under the cornice's soffit, while the cornice (the fit), the porte-cochere's footings and the principal storey's lights land within 5-10 px, so the second storey's sills are raised to 8.3 m here (heads 11.0 m); the principal storey's keep 2.6 m over 2.9 m. The principal storey's lights at s 21.5 and 24.5 remain reconstructed: the trees and the coping wall hide them. T-1881: the pair and the triple over the porte-cochere and the pair seen through its arches are on the 18th Street pavilion's front (bays.p_18th), not this wall; the lights at s 12.48-17.6 and 19.99-20.25 here are taken off. The east end's second-storey pair (s 22.78, 23.92; Taylor x 789-809 px on the main wall's plane) and the principal storey's reconstructed lights at s 21.5 and 24.5 stay.

sash_by_storey.note: Through the photograph's camera: the centre bay's second-storey window from about 7.8 to 10.5 m over grade (y 378 and 335 px at 16.0 px/m); the principal storey's, behind the ivy, are taken as tall.

chimneys.note: RECONSTRUCTED as a whole, its third stack read off a photograph (T-3161): the 18th Street flank's great stack is read off J. W. Taylor's photograph no. 1445 (the album print a16-aic-taylor-album-pullman-p69 and the print a16-aic-taylor-pullman-from-nw, one negative) through its solved camera (docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/pullman_house_1729_prairie/taylor-1445-camera.md; the prints are link-only in the library, so the camera waits on the rights question on T-3161 before it joins the image gate): a stone stack standing on the flank's cornice and carried up the mansard's face, x 487-522 px at its base on the cornice (y 272-292) against the corner pier at x 447: its west side and south face together 35 px, at 18 px a metre along the flank there and 19 px a metre across it, so a 1.1 m face on the flank's line at u 24.25-25.35 with its 0.8 m west side seen beside it; its moulded cap at y 160, 18.7 m through the camera (the curb at about 16.9 m), a band under the cap. The 1890 Albertype plate shows the same stack rising behind the tree just east of the corner pier. Its depth across the wall line is not measured: 0.8 m, standing on the cornice in front of the mansard's face (its inner face 0.14 m clear of the deck's curb at v 17.46, so the cresting runs behind it) with its outer face 0.47 m out, inside the 0.6 m cornice, as the photograph shows it standing proud of the slope. The deck stack at (20, 13.3) is read from the same three pictures: the Detroit print and the Albertype plate, both from the crossing's south-west corner, show a tall stack rising behind the cresting just WEST of the south-west corner pier (Detroit x 528-545 px, top y 222, against the corner at x 557-560; the plate x about 1293, top y 213, against its corner at 1312), which no stack on the flank's line can do from there; their common line of sight passes the deck at about u 20, v 13.3, where Taylor's camera hides a stack wholly behind the flank stack, as that photograph shows (it shows only cresting either side of it). Its top through the two cameras is 19.05 and 19.9 m, taken at 19.5 (top_m); its place along the line of sight is good to about 1.5 m. It was a reconstructed stack at (18, 12.5) until T-3161. The flank stack is not in the 1890 plate, which is earlier than Taylor's photograph (1890s, after the 1892 additions it shows east of the flank): it is read as later work and stands in 1904. The stack at (10, 5.5) remains RECONSTRUCTED: through all three cameras it stands under the deck's edge, so no picture shows or excludes it. L-pullman-1729-flank-stack-3161.

entrance_kit.note: The portico the sheet draws 3 m deep in front of the Prairie front (v 1.6 to 10.6), built as the door's hood on columns: the photograph's columned portico carrying a balustraded balcony at the second floor (y 380-395 px). T-3159, through the Detroit print's solved camera (data/reference_views/pullman_house_1729_prairie/detroit_det_4a08065.json; the portico's front at u 30.6, 13-14 px a metre): the portico is the front's brownstone, not painted joinery (fabric stone), its balcony railed by a stone balustrade (the print's posts and balusters at y 380-390 over the entablature at 390-400, x 343-395; railing_fabric stone, 0.7 m, its rail clear under the second-storey sills). Its columns: the print shows two clear of the ivy and the trees, a lit round shaft at x 374-381 (v 6.9) and one at x 322-330 (v 3.05), both standing on the portico's floor at y 470; the south half is lost in the ivy, so the row is carried on at the print's pitch, a column at the hood's south end (v 10.03) and one between (v 8.5), four in all (the count is the match record's 'four or more'; the two south positions are a bounded design, L-pullman-1729-portico-3159). The flight: the sheet's stoop (s20fp-1729-b1 p1-p2) is 2.6 x 3.4 m, and the print's steps (x 300-370, y 465-490) rise between the two read columns, its north cheek's raked top running from x 335 y 465 down to x 298 y 488 (v about 3.7): a 2.6 m flight centred at v 5.0 (stoop_v_m), and the rest of the portico's floor terraces at the landing's height either side of it out to the hood's ends. T-1881: the portico re-laid in front of the forward block (bays.p_forward): its hood 6.3 m wide centred at v 5.25, 1.2 m out from the block's face, its four columns at v 2.4, 4.25, 6.25 and 8.1, the flight centred at v 4.0 and the terrace from v 2.1 to 8.4. Through the Detroit print's camera the steps (x 300-370 px) read v 2.0-7.1 on the hood's front line, which the flight and its landing fill; the columns' places in the hood are reconstructed, evenly spaced (L-pullman-1729-portico-3159). T-1881 (the owner, 2026-10-29: the stair off the door's axis, its cheeks into the columns, a plain stone block beside it): the flight re-centred on the door at v 5.25 (stoop_v_m taken off; the stoop is the door's), and the two inner columns stood where the print reads its two, 3.9 m apart, re-centred on that axis (v 3.3 and 7.2, each within 0.3 m of the reading at 3.05 and 6.9), so the 2.6 m flight and its cheeks rise between their plinths with 0.35 m to spare each side; the outer two stand at the hood's ends (v 2.4 and 8.1) before the forward block's banded corner piers. A turned stone balustrade (balustrade, 0.9 m) runs on the cheeks, raked down the flight, and on the terraces' fronts either side, where the print draws a railing raked beside the steps (x 298-335 px on the north cheek, and its fellow on the south); its section is reconstructed. (L-pullman-1729-entry-axis-1881)
